When Margaret's husband died, she thought she was prepared.

But she soon realized she couldn't find most of his important documents anywhere.

They were buried somewhere in 30 years of filing cabinets. His will, his account passwords? Scribbled on sticky notes she couldn't find.

She spent THREE WEEKS drowning in paperwork while grieving. The bank froze accounts. Her kids watched her fall apart.

This happens to 75% of families. Not because they're careless... but because life gets busy and important documents end up scattered in a dozen different places.

If you need a creative outlet for your emotions, art therapy is the PERFECT thing to try in 2026.

Art therapy sounds like something that only happens in a therapist's office.

But here's the secret:

It's simply using art to calm your mind. A pencil and a sheet of paper. That's all you need.

The other secret?

You don't need any artistic talent. In a Drexel University study, 45 minutes of making art lowered the stress hormone cortisol in 75% of adults, whatever their art skills.
